SEND At Reading Girls' School, our SEND department is committed to ensuring that every student with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND) is given the opportunity to thrive academically, socially, and emotionally.

Our intent is to provide an inclusive, nurturing, and empowering environment where all students, regardless of their learning challenges, receive the individualised support they need to achieve their full potential.

Children and young people with an MSI have a combination of vision and hearing difficulties.' Code of Practice 2015 At Reading Girls' School, students with disabilities that make it challenging to access lessons—such as those with visual, hearing, or multisensory impairments—receive support from the SEND Department.
If you have questions, email our SENCO and Inclusion lead at senco@readinggirlsschool.net or visit Readings SEND local offer services webpage to see the support available in Reading.

RGS: Roadworks outside the school
We would like to make you aware that roadworks taking place outside the school for what the Council currently anticipates will be a two-week period. To help manage traffic flow during this time, temporary traffic lights will be in operation, including lights specifically controlling the exit from the RGS site. As a result, we expect there to be increased congestion around the school, particularly at the beginning and end of the school day. Where possible, we would advise parents and carers not to use the school car park during this period and to consider alternative arrangements for dropping off and collecting students. Should you choose to use the school car park, we kindly ask for your patience and understanding, as delays are likely while the roadworks are underway. We will continue to monitor the situation and provide any updates should further information become available. We apologise for any inconvenience this may cause and thank you for your cooperation and support.

Personal Development
We aim to grow our girls into sensible and confident young adults who are not only able to make reasoned and sensible decisions but are also able to participate fully in and contribute positively to life in modern Britain
Our coherent Personal Development programme now meets toolkit expectations for character, citizenship, equality and online safety. PSHE/RSE is sequenced across Y7–11 responding to the contextulised needs of our students. Personal Development and well-being was a key focus with the introduction of Academic mentoring time and assembly programme, House system and PSHE into the curriculum in 2023-2024 along with the revision of enrichment systems. Enrichment and educational visits are mapped to ensure breadth and progression, alongside co-curricular House competitions and events, nurturing pupils talents and interests.
Over 50 employer/university links provide authentic experiences; careers education meets all Gatsby Benchmarks. The in-depth careers programme supports students within their next steps of their education, 99.6% of school leavers with sustained destinations. Student leadership (Senior Student Leadership Team, form representatives, prefects and mental health ambassadors) builds agency and voice. Well-being is addressed through mentoring, counselling access, and curriculum content on health and well-being including healthy relationships and digital citizenship.
The Personal Development Programme encompasses the following strands:
Academic mentoring including the assembly programme
Spiralled PSHE curriculum
Personal Development Events
Enrichment Programme including clubs, educational visits, House events and other calendared events
Leadership opportunities including Form reps and student voice, Prefects and SSLT
Careers Education and Independent Advice and Guidance
STEM (Science, technology, engineering and maths)

SEND
At Reading Girls' School, our SEND department is committed to ensuring that every student with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND) is given the opportunity to thrive academically, socially, and emotionally. Our intent is to provide an inclusive, nurturing, and empowering environment where all students, regardless of their learning challenges, receive the individualised support they need to achieve their full potential.

If you have questions, email our SENCO and Inclusion lead at senco@readinggirlsschool.net or visit Readings SEND local offer services webpage to see the support available in Reading. You can also reach out to parent support groups or SEND advocates for additional guidance.
If you are concerned about your childs needs, please email senco@readinggirlsschool.net

What is SEND?
SEND stands for Special Educational Needs and Disabilities. Some children may need additional support at school due to learning difficulties, disabilities, or health issues that affect their learning and development. The SEND system helps schools and families work together to ensure every child gets the support they need.
What is the SEND Wave System?
The SEND Wave System is a framework that schools use to organise and provide support for children with SEND. It consists of three different "waves" or levels of support. These waves ensure that support is tailored to each child's individual needs.
Wave 1: Quality First Teaching
This is the foundation for all students, including those with SEND.
Wave 2: Targeted Support
For students who need more support than what Wave 1 provides.
Wave 3: Specialist Support
This is the highest level of support for children with more significant or complex needs.
How Does the School Decide Which Wave My Child Needs?
The school follows a graduated approach to determine what level of support your child needs:
If your child’s needs change, they may move between waves as required.
What is an Education, Health, and Care Plan (EHCP)?
An EHCP is a legal document for children who have more complex needs that can’t be fully met through regular classroom support. It outlines the child’s needs, the support they should receive, and the outcomes they are working towards. It involves input from parents, teachers, and specialists.

Physical & Sensory (P&S)
'Some children and young people require special educational provision because they have a disability which prevents or hinders them from making use of the educational facilities generally provided. These difficulties can be age related and may fluctuate over time. Many children and young people with vision impairment (VI), hearing impairment (HI) or a multi-sensory impairment (MSI) will require specialist support and/or equipment to access their learning, or habilitation support. Children and young people with an MSI have a combination of vision and hearing difficulties.'
Code of Practice 2015
At Reading Girls' School, students with disabilities that make it challenging to access lessons—such as those with visual, hearing, or multisensory impairments—receive support from the SEND Department. We work closely with external agencies to provide expert advice and recommendations to teaching staff on how to best accommodate these students through tailored differentiation.
Physical & Sensory needs can include:
Visual Impairment -is the partial or total inability of visual perception.
Hearing impairment - not able to hear as well as someone with normal hearing, meaning hearing thresholds of 20 dB
Multi-sensory impairment - Impairments in both sight and hearing.
Physical Disability - limitation on a person's physical functioning, mobility, dexterity or stamina having a substantial or long-term effect on their life.
Sensory processing disorder - a condition in which the brain has trouble receiving information from the senses this can cause anxiety and frustration.
Useful website links
Websites parents may find useful to support their child with P&S needs are:
Sensory needs - https://www.handinhandparenting.org/
https://standishfoundation.org/?
Visual impairments - https://www.rnib.org.uk/living-with-sight-loss
Hearing difficulties - https://kidshealth.org/en/parents/hearing-factsheet.html
